ideas.description: Exploit, a time-neutral accuracy booster. The tip's population mean is now below the bar (held-out 0.7526), so the next time cut needs one first. On the E027 tip (8.75 true epochs, 219 steps at batch 2000, 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%), change only the LR warm-up length. First read the current warm-up and peak fraction from the code (airbench96 uses a peak at about 0.23 of steps). Halve it so the peak comes earlier, with the same peak value and a linear decay to the same 0.07 floor, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups. The Lookahead/EMA ramp, resolution phases, epochs, wd and LS all stay unchanged. If LR is a GPU tensor, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture every resolution in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if the held-out gain is at least 0.15 pp and seeds 0–2 clear 0.753.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%, about 5.88 s). Held-out mean moves −0.15 to +0.3 pp from 0.7526, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.15 pp supports H1.6.1 and funds about 0.35 epoch or the 20 px extension (H2.3.6). A loss of at least 0.15 pp means the warm-up protects the Muon/BN-bias start in short runs, and the next point should be a later peak, not an earlier one.

ideas.description: Exploit, a time-neutral averaging booster in the direction opposite to E025 (which pulled harder and hurt by 0.27 pp held-out). D003 (C0024/C0025) points to the reset interval as the untuned Lookahead knob. On the E027 tip, change only the Lookahead update interval from every 5 to every 10 steps. Rescale the per-update retention so the total pull per step is unchanged (alpha_10 = alpha_5**2 at each ramp point, same exponent 3), and keep the final full copy. LR, epochs, resolution, wd and LS stay unchanged. Recapture the step graphs if the interval or alpha is baked in, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged or −0.3% (half as many Lookahead updates). Held-out mean moves −0.2 to +0.25 pp from 0.7526, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.15 pp supports H1.3.7 (fast weights need longer free runs), and the next point is every 20 steps. A loss of at least 0.15 pp means frequent pull-back is part of the gain, consistent with Switch-EMA, and closes H1.3's tuning branch.

ideas.description: Exploit, a time-neutral booster that targets the end-point, where averaging forms (E005 showed the late phase is worth about 1 pp). On the E027 tip, keep label smoothing at 0.3 for the first 85% of steps and set it to 0 for the final 15%, which lies entirely inside the 32 px phase. Pass LS as a GPU scalar into the compiled loss, or capture a second 32 px step variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Nothing else changes. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves −0.2 to +0.25 pp from 0.7526, median 0. A gain of at least 0.15 pp supports H1.3.8: late LS removal sharpens the 100-way head once features have formed. A loss of at least 0.15 pp means LS acts as end-point regularization that the Lookahead average relies on, and LS tuning should stop. (Global LS was flat between 0.2 and 0.3 in E013, so a phase-specific effect is the only remaining LS question.)

ideas.description: Exploit and crux test (W1/W5: is early low resolution close to free?). Run it on the E027 tip, or on the tip plus any booster above that was kept with at least +0.15 pp held-out. Change only the resolution split from 20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30% of steps to 30/10/30/30%. The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact step counts and positions, and the LR and Lookahead schedules are unchanged. The 20 px graph is already captured in build, and error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 and the held-out mean stays at or above 0.752 (the 40-seed official bar of 0.75 then has at least 0.2 pp of headroom).
ideas.expected: About 1.3 true epochs move from about 0.51 to about 0.36 s/epoch, so time falls 3–3.5% (about 0.18–0.2 s), to about 5.68–5.72 s. If early resolution is free, the held-out mean drops 0.1 pp or less, a rate of at least 2 s/pp, which beats the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp). If it repeats E026's rate (about 1.2 s/pp), it drops about 0.15 pp, which is no better than epochs. Then stop resizing and spend future time cuts on epochs.

ideas.description: Explore (W5 crux, a proposed new H2.3 child: the low-res cost is partly a stem-statistics mismatch). The frozen 2×2 patch-whitening conv is computed in prepare from 32 px patches. Downsampled 20/24/28 px images have higher per-pixel frequency content, so the frozen filter leaves their outputs non-white, and BN plus group 1 must re-adapt at every resolution jump. On the E027 tip, compute the whitening eigenbasis in prepare separately for each training resolution (from at most 5k training images resized with the same F.interpolate path, inside timed prepare). Use the matching frozen whitening weights in each phase. The 32 px weights stay the ones used at eval. The whitening bias is shared, and nothing else changes. Capture each resolution's graph in build with its own whitening buffer, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time +0.5–1% (three extra 12×12 eigendecompositions and patch extraction in prepare). Held-out mean moves −0.15 to +0.3 pp, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.2 pp supports the stem-mismatch child and suggests resolution cuts can go further once the stem is matched. A change within ±0.1 pp refutes it, which leaves (a) the peak-LR timing or (c) the tail length as the mechanisms behind H2.3's cost.

drop.reason: All four committee members forecast harm and none an improvement. Muon lr was flat between 0.24 and 0.36 (E014), and the change is time-neutral, so a gain would have to be ≥0.2 pp, beyond the forecast range. It also targets E023, which is no longer the tip.

The committee agrees (conflict 0): the step is GPU-bound, so batch 2500 saves only about 2%, while 20% fewer Muon and Lookahead steps in a short run likely costs at least 0.15 pp. That is no better than the epoch dial, and the tip's population margin (held-out 0.7526) cannot absorb a loss. The low-information outcome isn't worth a slot.

Low information: all four members forecast the same outcome (at least 90 TFLOP/s at 32 px, no kernel lever over 5%), and the diagnostic changes no recipe. Its main use was interpreting architecture cuts, and E021/E024 already gave the tile-alignment lesson. I043's measured time saving will answer the group-1 backward cost question directly.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E027: 5.88 s, seeds 0–2 at 0.7547. Its held-out mean is 0.7526, below the local bar of 0.753, though still about 0.26 pp above the official 40-seed bar of 0.75. Any further time cut has to be paid for with an accuracy gain first. The queue therefore leads with three time-neutral boosters on the E027 tip, all judged on held-out seeds:
- a shorter LR warm-up (H1.6.1, priority 5);
- a Lookahead reset every 10 steps instead of 5, with the total pull per step kept equal (H1.3.7, priority 4). This goes the opposite way from E025's harder pull, which hurt.
- label smoothing switched off for the last 15% of steps (H1.3.8, priority 3).

Two more ideas:
- **Exploit (priority 3):** extend the 20 px phase from 15% to 30% of steps (H2.3.6). This tests the W1/W5 crux of whether early low resolution is free. It should stack on any booster that is kept.
- **Explore (priority 2):** compute the frozen whitening conv separately for each training resolution. This tests W5's idea that part of the low-resolution cost is a mismatch in the first layer's statistics.

I044 (dropping easy examples using the main net's own per-sample losses) stays queued as an explore idea, and I043 (FreezeOut-style truncation) is still running.

Three ideas are dropped:
- **I046 (Muon lr ×2):** all four members forecast harm, and the lr has been flat in earlier runs.
- **I045 (batch 2500):** the members agree it saves only about 2% for a likely loss of at least 0.15 pp, which is no better than cutting epochs.
- **I040 (profiling diagnostic):** the members already agree on its outcome, so it would tell us little.

That leaves six queued ideas and one running.
